analysis.title: One Peak To Rule Them All: How The AI Hangover Runs Through Every One Of Goldman's 2027 Outlooks
key_insights: Goldman's five 2027 outlooks (macro, cross-asset, equity, FX, commodities) share one theme: nominal global AI investment rises from $1.1tn in 2026 to $1.8tn in 2027, but the year-over-year change as a share of GDP peaks in 1H27 and the level peaks in 2028.
AI explains 21% of US GDP growth, 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth and, at the peak, 92% of the gain in US market value. Goldman concludes the AI peak is a bigger test for markets than for the economy.

Macro: Goldman sees 2027 global growth of 2.8% ('remarkably unremarkable'), core PCE falling to 2.4%, two more Fed hikes (December and March), then a cut in December 2027 and a 3.25-3.5% terminal rate. Risks are skewed to the downside.
AI is estimated to add 0.2pp to measured US GDP growth in 2027 and 0.6pp to 'true' GDP after correcting for undercounted chip spending.

Equities: S&P 500 earnings growth is forecast to fall from 36% to 11%. Europe falls from about 18% to 7%, Japan from 24% to 9%, Asia from near 80% to under 30%. S&P target is 8,700 in 12 months (14% upside from 7,619). Overweight US and Japan, underweight Europe.

Oppenheimer's team says US forward P/E has fallen to 18.5x from near its 20-year 100th percentile. Hyperscalers trade at 19.7x, below the previous 20-year range and cheaper than Consumer Staples, and are the favored hiding spot. Goldman acknowledges the biggest companies have turned cash flow negative, though net debt/equity remains healthy.
Korea's memory sector is pricing a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings, which Goldman's Asia team calls excessive given sold-out DRAM and HBM products until 2029.

Credit: the economists count $687bn of AI-related debt issuance in 2026 plus $115bn of equity. Goldman forecasts US IG spreads widening from 88bp to 105bp and HY from 320bp to 410bp, and says it is hard to see US spreads tightening sharply. Goldman expects bifurcation between AI-related issuers and the rest.
Goldman argues stocks are less able to ignore credit widening than in 1998-2000, because the capital inflows and goods price deflation from the 1997-98 EM crises are absent.

Rates: the stock-bond correlation turned negative as AI replaced oil as the market's main fear. Goldman's 10Y target is 4.6% by end-2027, set against a 4.99% 10Y on Nov 11. The 10Y ended last week above 5.15%. The article notes this is dovish relative to market pricing.
Memory price forecasts were revised higher again this earnings season, which Goldman's economists say points to more near-term upside to core inflation from AI spillovers.
France: the OAT-Bund spread is about 150bp and real fiscal consolidation talk is unlikely before the April and June elections. Goldman's markets team still likes EUR downside optionality.

FX: Goldman finds Dollar performance linked to AI-related equity performance in good times and bad. It forecasts a roughly 3% fall in the broad Dollar in 2027, with EUR/USD sliding to 1.08 in three months then recovering to 1.15 by end-2027.

The Yen is about 30% undervalued, USD/JPY is seen at 150 in 12 months from 160, and Goldman calls the Yen the clearest beneficiary of a deeper challenge to the AI outlook. USD/CNY is seen at 6.30 by end-2027, about 22% undervalued.

Commodities: the Brent risk premium has dropped from $27 before the midterms to a few dollars. Base case is Brent averaging $88 in 2027 and ending at $78. Upside scenario is Brent above $130 in early 2027, and the economists' adverse case at $132 adds 0.9pp to headline inflation.

Goldman warns a renewed supply shock could bring lower bond prices and lower equities, the one scenario where bonds do not hedge stocks. Over six decades, in every 12-month stretch when both stocks and bonds lost money in real terms, gold or broad commodities made money.
Goldman targets gold at $4,650 and copper at $15,600 by December 2027, with energy hedges in June 2027 European gasoline and Q1 TTF call spreads.
Hedge list across the outlooks: long US and Japanese duration, short USD/JPY, long longer-dated equity calls instead of stock, TTF call spreads, and a slice of commodities.

ZeroHedge's own view (not Goldman's): the downside path is more likely, given a Fed still hiking, the biggest net equity supply since 2000, cracking credit at the AI edges, and an economy tied to the stock market.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's baseline is benign: 2.8% global growth, 11% EPS growth, falling inflation and a Fed cutting by December 2027. The US forward P/E at 18.5x and Hyperscalers at 19.7x already reflect much of the slowdown, supporting an 8,700 S&P target.
tension_points.bear_case: AI explains 62% of S&P earnings growth and up to 92% of market value gains against 21% of GDP growth, so a peak in growth rates hits markets harder than the economy. Credit spreads are widening, hyperscaler free cash flow has deteriorated, and the Fed is hiking.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed oil supply shock (Brent above $130) or signs that AI investment growth is peaking faster in 1H27 would break the benign baseline, and a stock-bond selloff would remove the bond hedge.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees the 10Y at 4.6% by end-2027, citing running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and a dovish Fed path, with the stock-bond correlation negative.
tension_points.bear_case: The 10Y has moved against the target, from 4.99% on Nov 11 to above 5.15%, driven by hot CPI and AI-related memory price inflation. A renewed supply shock could hurt bonds and stocks together.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed oil supply shock that lowers bond and equity prices together, as in 2026, would break the bond-as-hedge case.
